To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collaborative sensing is a promising solution for opportunistic access to spectrum in fading environments.

1) the proposed collaborative spectrum sensing scheme can improve the sensing performance of the secondary users, 2) the performance of the proposed collaborative spectrum scheme is dependent on the number of secondary users and the number of sensing slots and 3) there is an optimal number of users that can be selected to improve the sensing performance.
• In a fading channel, a secondary user may not be able to detect the absence of primary signal and hence transmit in a licensed band.
In summary, our research is concerned with
spectrum sensing and sharing in fading environment.

the following questions: How to enable access to spectrum that is not currently being used by primary licensee? Can secondary users access spectrum opportunistically? How does the sensing performance change when the number of sensors increase?
the design and analysis of spectrum sensing algorithms for opportunistic spectrum access in fading environments and with the development of a framework for collaborative spectrum sensing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed collaborative spectrum sensing is an efficient way for secondary users to detect the presence of a primary user.
the proposed collaborative spectrum-sensing scheme is able to improve sensing performance significantly.
collaborative spectrum sensing is a viable and promising solution to the spectrum scarcity problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and evaluated an efficient and practical spectrum sensing scheme for opportunistic spectrum access.
we have studied a spectrum-sharing scenario where a primary system and a secondary user co-exist in the same band.
we study the performance of a cognitive radio network with a primary user and a secondary network with multiple users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collaborative spectrum sensing may be a promising solution to the problem of opportunistic spectrum access in fading channels.
collaboration is a viable solution for spectrum-sharing in fading environments and may be used to improve the performance of secondary users.
spectrum sensing is feasible in fading environments, and that collaborative sensing may improve the performance of secondary users.
